summary: Bob completes his transfer into the upgraded Heaven-1A and brings four new replicants online. Bob says their former booby-traps and imperatives have been removed, and Riker, Bill, Milo, and Mario quickly choose different names and priorities as the new HEAVEN vessels take on manufacturing and shakedown work. Bill remains in-system to oversee production and investigate an unexpected SUDDAR result, while Bob's proposal for early terraforming on EE-2 and the others' possible journeys make clear that the copies are already pursuing distinct paths.

introducing.name: relay station
introducing.description: An automated station intended for every system Bob visits. It can send encrypted status reports and planetary surveys to Earth, and, when colonization is viable, serve as a beacon, communications relay, and in-system hub; it is to have an AMI and limited manufacturing capability.

updates.current_state: At Epsilon Eridani in Heaven-1A after completing a hardware transfer and bringing four new replicants online.

updates.description: A converted interplanetary freighter equipped as a Von Neumann probe: a small, light, resilient design built to copy itself. It carries a SURGE drive ring, fusion reactor, ramscoop, three large 3D printers, ROAMers, nanites and mining cargo carriers, but no weapons. Version-2 HEAVENs add a larger reactor and drive, a rail-gun, ship-busters, bigger replicant systems and more cargo room. Its communications report to Earth and were not built for interstellar conversation.

GUPPI, the General Unit Primary Peripheral Interface, offloads tasks for replicants, who keep human limits on multitasking. Its operating system is firmware, so changing its replication priority would require a new core and ship. Version 2 has enough memory that a personality matrix is contemplated.

A subspace detection technology enabled by the same breakthrough as the SURGE drive. It can monitor distance, scan for threats and detect dense objects within a light-hour. An emitter flaw can give a much weaker ping with poor close-range sensitivity, which Bill suspects may reach farther.
A spare hardware unit carried aboard Heaven-1 that can contain a complete GUPPI system.

Remote observation and manipulation devices directed through GUPPI. They come in varied sizes, coordinate across scales and, once their tasks are defined, need little supervision. They can inspect ship circuitry with gnat-sized units, carry video cameras and pick up vibrations through a wall. Running on reusable scripts, they feed ore to manufacturing systems, gather parts and assemble ships, and printers can make more of them.

A planet orbiting at 0.85 AU, about 90 percent of Earth's size, with comparatively little water. Its isolated seas cover about 30 percent of the surface and are surrounded by land. Its atmosphere contains about 3 percent oxygen, which may reflect photosynthetic life in the seas or a natural process. Bare rock shows no green, while snow, polar ice, and morning frost reach the equator. It seems barely livable, though people could probably live there with substantial technological assistance such as domes; its atmosphere and water make it comparatively favorable against Mars. A described small moon is noted. Bob proposes early terraforming by directing Kuiper objects inward to increase the oceans.
